results.evidence: The new test inserts claim_verified rows for an other-claim payload and for the malformed payload {"claim_id": "service-area"} (no verifier, no date). It also inserts a valid service-area row, and the valid row is inserted first, so every row to skip is newer and is read first. It asserts standing_verification(conn, 'service-area') == Verification(valid_id, 'Founder', '2026-11-30'), which covers the id, verified_by and verified_at. standing_verification (cottonwood/claims.py:109-125) skips rows for other claim ids and rows without string verified_by and verified_at, so the test exercises that loop. The test file has two extra malformed payloads (non-string date, non-object) and two extra tests (all-skipped returns None, and other-claim's row still counts for its own claim). All 3 tests pass with pytest. I did not run a mutant, so I did not confirm that the test fails when the skip logic is broken.
results.quote:
def test_the_valid_row_is_found_past_later_rows_it_must_skip(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    valid_id = _insert(conn, json.dumps(VALID))
    for payload in NOISE:  # every row to skip is newer, so it is read first
        _insert(conn, payload)
    found = claims.standing_verification(conn, "service-area")
    assert found == claims.Verification(valid_id, "Founder", "2026-11-30")

results.evidence: test_only_rows_to_skip_give_no_standing_verification inserts only the NOISE rows (an other-claim row plus malformed payloads: missing verifier/date, non-string date, non-object) and asserts standing_verification(conn, 'service-area') is None. standing_verification (cottonwood/claims.py:109-125) skips rows whose claim_id differs (line 119) and returns a result only when verified_by and verified_at are both strings (line 123), so it falls through to None (line 125). The test run passed 3/3. One caveat: the non-object payload relies on _payload() returning a dict-like value, and that passed in the run.
